comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims C1, C8, C9. Both evaluations support these well-established efficient coding principles with extensive citations. OpenEval notes they 'accurately represent prior work,' while peer reviewers acknowledge the 'established theoretical framework' without challenge.

Significant disagreement on claims C5, C23, C24, C37, C41 regarding E:I ratio predictions. OpenEval finds these 'well-supported by parameter optimization' with values in 'empirically observed ranges.' Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting the 4:1 ratio 'hinges on somewhat arbitrary hyperparameter choices' and questioning whether efficient coding truly accounts for biological properties or is merely 'flexible enough to be consistent.'

Agreement on claims C18, C35 regarding adaptation effects. Both evaluations support findings that optimal adaptation time constants eliminate adaptation. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of spike-triggered adaptation, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'sensible constraints' maintaining 'good properties.'

Agreement on claims C7, C25 regarding stimulus timescale robustness. OpenEval demonstrates 'stable performance across two orders of magnitude,' while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the 'convincing' comprehensive characterization without raising concerns.

Agreement on claim C21 regarding firing rate scaling with neuron number. Both evaluations support the predicted linear relationship. OpenEval notes consistency with empirical observations, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the thorough parameter exploration.

Agreement on claims C27, C28, C29, C30 comparing E-I and single cell-type models. Both evaluations support the robustness advantage of E-I architecture. OpenEval details specific performance differences, while peer reviewers view this as 'important contribution' showing networks 'can be modified to be much closer to biophysical reality.'

Agreement on claim C32 regarding inhibitory neuron selectivity. Both evaluations support that I neurons acquire selectivity through structured E-I connections. OpenEval provides quantitative selectivity index analysis, while peer reviewers treat this as expected outcome of model structure.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C17, C33, C34 regarding structured vs. unstructured network advantages. OpenEval finds 'consistent advantages of structured connectivity' with systematic comparisons. Peer reviewers accept this as key contribution, noting 'sensible constraints' and 'good properties.' Peer result also includes C39 on balance-efficiency relationship.

Agreement on claims C15, C16 regarding photostimulation simulations and feature competition. Both evaluations support that structured connectivity produces lateral inhibition patterns matching experimental observations. OpenEval notes 'qualitative reproduction' of Chettih and Harvey findings, while peer reviewers affirm 'experimentally observed phenomenon of feature competition.'

Agreement on claims C20, C44, C45, C46, C47, C49 regarding noise effects and optimal noise levels. Both evaluations support systematic noise analysis findings. OpenEval details 'optimal noise at non-zero levels' and correlation between parameters, while peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive parameter exploration studying 'role of many free parameters in depth.'

Agreement on claim C40 regarding spike decorrelation. OpenEval demonstrates 'weak spike timing coordination despite shared inputs,' while peer reviewers accept balance and decorrelation as core contributions addressing 'long-standing puzzles about neural circuits.' Peer result also addresses C38 on instantaneous balance.

Agreement on claim C42 regarding absence of E-E connections. Both evaluations support this as model feature with acknowledged limitations. OpenEval notes analytical derivation and authors' acknowledgment of simplification, while peer reviewers explicitly note 'revised manuscript is more transparent about the model's limitations' including lack of E-E connectivity.

Agreement on claim C43 regarding connection probability. Both evaluations support the 0.5 connection probability with acknowledged limitations for I-to-E connectivity. OpenEval notes match with E-to-I measurements but likely overestimation of I-to-E, while peer reviewers accept this as model limitation alongside C42.

Agreement on claims C12, C13, C14 regarding firing rate distributions. OpenEval supports these with simulation results matching empirical ranges and log-normal fits. Peer result groups these with broader model validation claims (C2, C3, C5, C6, C31), affirming model 'adds biological realism' and is 'consistent with multiple experimentally observed properties.'

Partial overlap on claim C10 regarding network size. OpenEval supports this as part of broader model validation (with C2, C31) showing parameters in 'biologically plausible ranges.' Peer reviewers accept network size as 'reasonable modeling decision' without challenge.

Partial overlap on claims C19, C36, C48 regarding metabolic constant optimization. OpenEval supports optimal β=14 mV with comparison to empirical data. Peer result addresses broader parameter exploration including these claims, accepting findings as part of comprehensive investigation of 'various (hyper)parameters' and 'role of many free parameters.'

Partial overlap on claims C6, C38 regarding instantaneous balance. OpenEval supports moderate instantaneous balance correlating with efficiency (C6, C38, C39). Peer result focuses on C38, C40, highlighting 'tight instantaneous balance' as key feature and accepting balance-efficiency relationship as core contribution without challenge.

Partial overlap on claims C2, C31 regarding model parameter validation. OpenEval supports these with analytical derivation and parameter optimization showing 'biologically plausible ranges.' Peer result groups these with broader validation claims (C3, C5, C6, C12-C14), affirming model is 'consistent with multiple experimentally observed properties' with 'convincing' analysis.

Minimal overlap on claim C39 regarding balance and efficiency. OpenEval supports that instantaneous balance correlates with network efficiency (C6, C38, C39). Peer result addresses structured network advantages (C4, C17, C33, C34, C39), accepting balance-efficiency relationship as part of key contribution showing 'sensible constraints' maintaining 'good properties.'

Minimal overlap on claim C3 regarding photostimulation. OpenEval supports C3 with simulated experiments reproducing empirical findings (with C15, C16). Peer result groups C3 with broader model validation (C2, C5, C6, C12-C14, C31), affirming model shows 'efficient coding explains, or at least is consistent with, multiple experimentally observed properties.'
